question.text: Given that $r$, $s$ and $t$ in the above diagram are parallel, find $m\angle 1.$
question.explanation:
Consider $\angle 2$ in the diagram below.

Notice that $\angle 2$ and the angle whose measure is $42^\circ$ are alternate exterior angles formed when the transversal $u$ cuts the parallel lines $r$ and $s.$ Hence, \[ m\angle 2 = 42^{\circ}. \]

Also, notice that the angle determined by $\angle 1$ and $\angle 2$ and the angle whose measure is $108^\circ$ are corresponding angles formed when the transversal $v$ cuts the parallel lines $s$ and $t.$ Hence, \[ m\angle 1 + m\angle 2 = 108^{\circ}. \]

Now, substituting $m\angle 2$ into the equation, we can find $m\angle1 \mathbin{:}$ \begin{align*} m\angle 1 + m\angle 2 & = 108^{\circ} \\[5pt] m\angle 1 + 42^\circ & = 108^{\circ} \\[5pt] m\angle 1 & = 66^{\circ} \end{align*}

question.explanation:
Consider $\angle 2$ in the diagram below.

Notice that $\angle 2$ and the angle whose measure is $66^\circ$ are alternate exterior angles formed when the transversal $v$ cuts the parallel lines $r$ and $s.$ Hence, \[ m\angle 2 = 66^{\circ}. \]

Also, notice that the angle determined by $\angle 1$ and $\angle 2$ and the angle whose measure is $127^\circ$ are corresponding angles formed when the transversal $u$ cuts the parallel lines $s$ and $t.$ Hence, \[ m\angle 1 + m\angle 2 = 127^{\circ}. \]

Now, substituting $m\angle 2$ into the equation, we can find $m\angle1 \mathbin{:}$ \begin{align*} m\angle 1 + m\angle 2 & = 127^{\circ} \\[5pt] m\angle 1 + 66^\circ & = 127^{\circ} \\[5pt] m\angle 1 & = 61^{\circ} \end{align*}

question.text: Given that $\overleftrightarrow{AB} \parallel \overleftrightarrow{CF},$ what is the measure of $\angle AFB?$
question.explanation:
Notice that $\angle{BAF}$ and $\angle{AFC}$ are alternate interior angles formed when the transversal $\overleftrightarrow{AF}$ cuts the parallel lines $\overleftrightarrow{AB}$ and $\overleftrightarrow{CF}.$ Hence, \[ m\angle{AFC} = m\angle{BAF} = 71^{\circ}. \]

Also, notice that $\angle{FBE}$ and $\angle{BFC}$ are alternate interior angles formed when the transversal $\overleftrightarrow{BF}$ cuts the parallel lines $\overleftrightarrow{AB}$ and $\overleftrightarrow{CF}.$ Hence, \[ m\angle{BFC} =m\angle{FBE} = 139^{\circ}. \]

Now, using the angle addition postulate, we can find $\angle{AFB}{:}$ \begin{align*} m \angle{AFB} & = m \angle{BFC} - m \angle{AFC} \\[5pt] & = 139^{\circ} - 71^{\circ} \\[5pt] & = 68^{\circ} \end{align*}
